newsitem.title: USA: Report on July US West power outage seen next week.
newsitem.headline: Report on July US West power outage seen next week.

text.p: A final report from the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) on the widespread power outage which hit the western U.S. on July 2 will likely be released next Thursday, said spokeswoman Corry Alsberg.

A preliminary report on the more severe August 10 outage was sent today for review by the council's board of trustees and operations committee, and members will have until next Friday to comment on it, she added.
A final report on the August outage is expected by mid-October, said Alsberg.

Since August 10, southbound transmissions on the Pacific Intertie have been restricted to 65 percent of capacity. The AC portion was capped at 3,200 megawatts (MW) of its 4,800-MW capacity, while the DC line has been limited to 2,000 of its 3,200 MW.
The restrictions are expected to remain in place until Bonneville and other operators "understand and correct voltage instability problems," said Perry Gruber, the BPA spokesman.
He said voltage instability was cropping up across the U.S. as the electric power industry begins to deregulate and transmission line usage increases.
"It is unclear to our experts exactly why it is happening," Gruber said.
